Subject: Performance SLO qualification / cost & perf levers | Acme AI | recap + next steps

Alex | thanks for the call today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment on the SLOs and the set of levers we'll validate in the benchmark run.

1) Target SLOs (what you shared):
- Latency: p95 <= 150ms for streaming responses on 512-token outputs
- Throughput: sustained 200 req/s at peak (burst to 500 req/s allowed)
- Concurrency: ~50 concurrent active sessions
- Availability: 99.9% (we'll map to Redwood Dedicated SLA options for production)

2) Constraints / important notes you called out:
- Most requests are streaming chat (token-by-token) to end users | preserving streaming latency is critical.
- Typical prompt length ~60 tokens, response avg ~320 tokens, 95th ~512 tokens.
- Payload size (input tokens) varies; will share a sample payload dump.

3) Cost / performance levers we propose to evaluate (we'll run these combinatorially in a small benchmark):
- Continuous batching (shape-aware batching to increase GPU utilization without hurting p95 streaming latency)
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and common prefixes (likely large win for chat reuse)
- Quantization profiles: int8 / fp16 tradeoffs; evaluate quality delta on your eval prompts against perf gains
- Model variants: \"redwood-2-large\" vs \"redwood-2-medium-quant\" (we'll include a lower-cost variant for graceful degradation)
- Dynamic routing: warm-standby for low-latency paths and fallback to cheaper variants during bursts

4) Data we need from your side to scope the run:
- Sample payloads (10-20 representative chats with token counts) | ideally anonymized JSONL
- Expected qps distribution (5m/1h/24h windows) and burst patterns
- Any strict regulatory constraints (no external telemetry)

5) Proposed next steps / timeline:
- You: share sample payloads + current qps dashboard link (by Mon 11/23)
- Redwood (Rishi): size benchmark infra and propose benchmark plan (deliverable: redwood_benchmark-plan.pdf) | by Tue 11/24
- Redwood (Priyom): run initial pilot (continuous batching + int8 quant) and share results + cost delta | target Fri 11/27
- Follow-up sync: 11/30 11:00 PT to review results and recommend production config

I've attached a cost-model template and a rough benchmark plan to help frame tradeoffs. Let us know if anything above is off.

Thanks —

Thanks Marissa | this looks right and captures the priorities. A few clarifications: 

- Confirming p95 target is for end-to-end streaming latency (token-first-byte to final token is less important than time-to-first-token for UX). So we care most about tail time-to-first-token (TTFT).
- Bursts: our flash-sale flows spike to ~450 req/s for ~3-5 minutes; after that it drops back.
- Regulatory: we can share anonymized telemetry; we're fine with Redwood running benchmarks in a redwood-dedicated test project with masked data.

I'll upload a 20-chat sample JSONL and a link to our Grafana panel by Monday COB. Also attaching the internal latency dashboard snapshot here: acme_latency_dashboard_20261119.png (attachment stub).

Agree on the timeline. For the model variants, we'd like Redwood to include a lower-cost quantized option as fallback if quality delta is <2% on our eval prompts.

Appreciate the clear next steps | looking forward to the pilot.

Looping in a very short tech note for the benchmark plan:

- Pilot config to validate: 
  * Model set: redwood-2-large (fp16), redwood-2-medium-quant (int8)
  * Batching: continuous batching with max batch size 64, latency-aware cutoff at 80ms to preserve TTFT
  * Caching: prefix-level KV cache for system prompts + conversation-level short-term cache (TTL 2m)
  * Streaming: chunked token flush every 40ms (tunable) to balance TTFT vs throughput
  * Concurrency shaping: reserve 20% capacity for low-latency path (no batching) during bursts

- Metrics we'll capture in the pilot: TTFT p50/p95/p99, end-to-end p95, GPU utilization, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and quality delta on Acme eval set (we'll compute ROUGE/embedding-sim scores you provide).

- Quick risks: int8 quant can reduce throughput variance but may introduce small hallucination regressions on long-form completion. We'll include a human-eval pass on 50 examples to surface any regression >2%.

I'll finalize the benchmark infra sizing once we get the sample payloads + qps distribution. I'll also draft the exact perf matrix to populate redwood_benchmark-plan.pdf.

Rishi
